theory.intro: Most rate problems involve only two quantities. A **related rates** problem involves three or more — for example drops, volume and time. Two of the rates are given and they are **chained together** by the quantity they share, so that the shared unit cancels and the rate you want is left.
facts: The shared quantity (Quantity 3) appears once on the top and once on the bottom, so it cancels.
Write the units in every fraction — they tell you whether the chain has been set up the right way round.
Convert all units before multiplying, both so they match each other and so they match the units the question asks for.
A common application is the **drip rate** for medication: $\dfrac{\text{drops}}{\text{min}} = \dfrac{\text{drops}}{\text{mL}} \times \dfrac{\text{mL}}{\text{min}}$.
steps: Identify the three quantities in the question
Set up a related rate equation
Convert the units to match each other and the units asked for

foundation.question_text: A patient is to receive $1.4$ L of fluid over $7$ hours through a drip giving $15$ drops/mL. How many drops per minute are required?
foundation.solution_text:
$\dfrac{\text{drops}}{\text{time}} = \dfrac{\text{drops}}{\text{volume}} \times \dfrac{\text{volume}}{\text{time}}$
$= \dfrac{15\text{ drops}}{1\text{ mL}} \times \dfrac{1400\text{ mL}}{420\text{ min}}$
$= \dfrac{15 \times 1400}{420}$
$= 50$
The rate is $50$ drops/min.

foundation.question_text: A patient is to receive $900$ mL of fluid over $6$ hours through a drip giving $15$ drops/mL. How many drops per minute are required, to the nearest drop?
foundation.solution_text:
$\dfrac{\text{drops}}{\text{time}} = \dfrac{\text{drops}}{\text{volume}} \times \dfrac{\text{volume}}{\text{time}}$
$= \dfrac{15\text{ drops}}{1\text{ mL}} \times \dfrac{900\text{ mL}}{360\text{ min}}$
$= \dfrac{15 \times 900}{360}$
$= 37.5$
The rate is $38$ drops/min.

foundation.question_text: How long will it take to deliver $600$ mL at $15$ drops/min if there are $10$ drops/mL? Give your answer in hours and minutes.
foundation.solution_text:
$\dfrac{\text{time}}{\text{volume}} = \dfrac{\text{time}}{\text{drops}} \times \dfrac{\text{drops}}{\text{volume}}$
$= \dfrac{1\text{ min}}{15\text{ drops}} \times \dfrac{10\text{ drops}}{1\text{ mL}}$
$= \dfrac{10\text{ min}}{15\text{ mL}}$
$x = \dfrac{10}{15} \times 600$
$= 400$ min
It takes $400$ minutes, which is $6$ h $40$ min.

foundation.question_text: How long will it take to deliver $1.2$ L at $25$ drops/min if there are $20$ drops/mL?
foundation.solution_text:
$1.2$ L $= 1200$ mL
$\dfrac{\text{time}}{\text{volume}} = \dfrac{\text{time}}{\text{drops}} \times \dfrac{\text{drops}}{\text{volume}}$
$= \dfrac{1\text{ min}}{25\text{ drops}} \times \dfrac{20\text{ drops}}{1\text{ mL}}$
$= \dfrac{20\text{ min}}{25\text{ mL}}$
$x = \dfrac{20}{25} \times 1200$
$= 960$ min
It takes $960$ minutes, which is $16$ hours.

foundation.question_text: A car uses $8.2$ L of fuel per $100$ km and fuel costs $\$1.85$ per litre. What is the fuel cost per kilometre, to the nearest tenth of a cent?
foundation.solution_text:
$\dfrac{\text{cost}}{\text{distance}} = \dfrac{\text{cost}}{\text{fuel}} \times \dfrac{\text{fuel}}{\text{distance}}$
$= \dfrac{\$1.85}{1\text{ L}} \times \dfrac{8.2\text{ L}}{100\text{ km}}$
$= \dfrac{\$15.17}{100\text{ km}}$
$= \dfrac{\$0.152}{1\text{ km}}$
The fuel costs $\$0.152$ per km.

foundation.question_text: A coffee shop buys coffee beans in $5$ kg bags for $\$45$ each. Each cup of coffee uses $12$ g of beans. What is the cost of beans per cup, to the nearest tenth of a cent?
foundation.solution_text:
$5$ kg $= 5000$ g
$\dfrac{\text{cost}}{\text{cup}} = \dfrac{\text{cost}}{\text{beans}} \times \dfrac{\text{beans}}{\text{cup}}$
$= \dfrac{\$45}{5000\text{ g}} \times \dfrac{12\text{ g}}{1\text{ cup}}$
$= \dfrac{\$0.108}{1\text{ cup}}$
The beans cost $\$0.108$ per cup.

development.question_text: What is the drip rate per minute for $850$ mL of fluid over $5$ hours with a drip size giving $8$ drops/mL? Answer to the nearest drop.
development.solution_text:
$\dfrac{\text{drops}}{\text{time}} = \dfrac{\text{drops}}{\text{volume}} \times \dfrac{\text{volume}}{\text{time}}$
$= \dfrac{8\text{ drops}}{1\text{ mL}} \times \dfrac{850\text{ mL}}{300\text{ min}}$
$= \dfrac{8 \times 850}{300}$
$= 22.6\ldots$
The rate is $23$ drops/min.

development.question_text: A patient is to receive $800$ mL of liquid through a drip delivering $25$ drops/min. If there are $16$ drops/mL, how long will it take to deliver the dose? Give your answer in hours and minutes.
development.solution_text:
$\dfrac{\text{time}}{\text{volume}} = \dfrac{\text{time}}{\text{drops}} \times \dfrac{\text{drops}}{\text{volume}}$
$= \dfrac{1\text{ min}}{25\text{ drops}} \times \dfrac{16\text{ drops}}{1\text{ mL}}$
$= \dfrac{16\text{ min}}{25\text{ mL}}$
$x = \dfrac{16}{25} \times 800$
$= 512$ min
$512 \div 60 = 8.5\dot{3}$ h
It takes $8$ h $32$ min.

development.question_text: Ruth's tropical fish breed at a rate of $8$ new fry every $2$ days per female fish. Ruth has $9$ female fish. How long will it take them to produce a total of $90$ new fry?
development.solution_text:
Rate per fish: $\dfrac{8\text{ fry}}{2\text{ days}} = \dfrac{4\text{ fry}}{1\text{ day}}$
Rate for $9$ fish: $\dfrac{4\text{ fry}}{1\text{ day}} \times 9 = \dfrac{36\text{ fry}}{1\text{ day}}$
$\dfrac{36\text{ fry}}{1\text{ day}} = \dfrac{90\text{ fry}}{x\text{ days}}$
$x = \dfrac{90}{36}$
$= 2.5$
It takes $2.5$ days.

development.question_text: Three painters together paint $180$ m$^{2}$ of fencing in $4$ hours. Working at the same rate each, how long would $5$ painters take to paint $375$ m$^{2}$?
development.solution_text:
Rate per painter: $\dfrac{180\text{ m}^{2}}{3\text{ painters} \times 4\text{ h}} = \dfrac{15\text{ m}^{2}}{1\text{ painter-hour}}$
Rate for $5$ painters: $\dfrac{15\text{ m}^{2}}{1\text{ painter-hour}} \times 5 = \dfrac{75\text{ m}^{2}}{1\text{ h}}$
$\dfrac{75\text{ m}^{2}}{1\text{ h}} = \dfrac{375\text{ m}^{2}}{x\text{ h}}$
$x = \dfrac{375}{75}$
$= 5$
It takes $5$ hours.

development.question_text: A printer uses $1.2$ mL of ink per page. Ink cartridges hold $60$ mL and cost $\$38$ each. What is the ink cost per page, to the nearest cent?
development.solution_text:
$\dfrac{\text{cost}}{\text{page}} = \dfrac{\text{cost}}{\text{ink}} \times \dfrac{\text{ink}}{\text{page}}$
$= \dfrac{\$38}{60\text{ mL}} \times \dfrac{1.2\text{ mL}}{1\text{ page}}$
$= \dfrac{\$0.76}{1\text{ page}}$
The ink costs $\$0.76$ per page.

development.question_text: A $24$ kg bag of flour costs $\$21.50$ and a sponge cake uses $150$ g of flour. What does the calculation $\dfrac{21.50}{24\,000} \times 150$ find?
development.solution_text:
$\dfrac{\$21.50}{24\,000\text{ g}} \times \dfrac{150\text{ g}}{1\text{ cake}}$
The units are $\dfrac{\$}{\text{g}} \times \dfrac{\text{g}}{\text{cake}}$, and the grams cancel to leave $\dfrac{\$}{\text{cake}}$.
It finds the cost of the flour used in one cake, which is about $\$0.13$.

mastery.question_text: A patient needs $0.75$ g of medicine per day. Pills contain $125$ mg each and cost $75$ c per pill. What is the annual cost of the medicine, in dollars? Use a $365$-day year.
mastery.solution_text:
$\dfrac{\text{cost}}{\text{time}} = \dfrac{\text{medicine}}{\text{time}} \times \dfrac{\text{pills}}{\text{medicine}} \times \dfrac{\text{cost}}{\text{pill}}$
$= \dfrac{750\text{ mg}}{1\text{ day}} \times \dfrac{1\text{ pill}}{125\text{ mg}} \times \dfrac{\$0.75}{1\text{ pill}}$
$= \dfrac{\$4.50}{1\text{ day}}$
$= \dfrac{\$4.50 \times 365}{1\text{ year}}$
$= \dfrac{\$1642.50}{1\text{ year}}$
The annual cost is $\$1642.50$.

mastery.question_text: A factory produces $25$ widgets in $4$ minutes. Each widget uses $15$ g of plastic, and plastic costs $\$3.20$ per kg. What is the plastic cost per hour?
mastery.solution_text:
$\dfrac{\text{cost}}{\text{time}} = \dfrac{\text{widgets}}{\text{time}} \times \dfrac{\text{plastic}}{\text{widget}} \times \dfrac{\text{cost}}{\text{plastic}}$
$= \dfrac{25\text{ widgets}}{4\text{ min}} \times \dfrac{0.015\text{ kg}}{1\text{ widget}} \times \dfrac{\$3.20}{1\text{ kg}}$
$= \dfrac{25 \times 60\text{ widgets}}{4\text{ h}} \times \dfrac{0.015\text{ kg}}{1\text{ widget}} \times \dfrac{\$3.20}{1\text{ kg}}$
$= \dfrac{375\text{ widgets}}{1\text{ h}} \times \dfrac{\$0.048}{1\text{ widget}}$
$= \dfrac{\$18}{1\text{ h}}$
The plastic costs $\$18$ per hour.

mastery.question_text: Mr Ding prints a $25$-sheet booklet for each of his $80$ students once every two weeks, for $38$ weeks. Printing paper comes in reams of $500$ sheets costing $\$9$ each. How much does the paper cost for the year?
mastery.solution_text:
Printings in the year: $38 \div 2 = 19$
Sheets per printing: $80 \times 25 = 2000$ sheets
Sheets per year: $2000 \times 19 = 38\,000$ sheets
$\dfrac{\text{cost}}{\text{year}} = \dfrac{38\,000\text{ sheets}}{1\text{ year}} \times \dfrac{1\text{ ream}}{500\text{ sheets}} \times \dfrac{\$9}{1\text{ ream}}$
$= \dfrac{76\text{ reams}}{1\text{ year}} \times \dfrac{\$9}{1\text{ ream}}$
$= \dfrac{\$684}{1\text{ year}}$
The paper costs $\$684$ for the year.
